title: Python Workers Reach GA on Cloudflare, with Questions About Cold Starts and Upstream Maintenance
gist: Cloudflare made Python Workers GA via Pyodide/WebAssembly, enabled by PEP 783 (PyEmscripten) packaging, a syscall-level socket bridge and upstream HTTP-client changes, while critics question cold starts (Wasmer claims ~60ms vs ~900ms), version coupling, memory use and the funding of upstream maintainers like urllib3.

insights.claim: Cloudflare made Python Workers generally available two years after first preview, alongside JavaScript and TypeScript, with bindings to Workers AI, R2, D1, Hyperdrive, Durable Objects, Queues and Workflows and support for FastAPI, Django and Flask.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Expands Cloudflare's developer platform addressable market to the large Python and AI developer base.

insights.claim: Upstream changes make requests and httpx route through the JavaScript fetch API in WebAssembly, which lets OpenAI, LangChain and MCP run inside a Worker.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Positions Cloudflare Workers as a runtime for Python AI agent workloads.

insights.claim: Cloudflare implemented POSIX socket syscalls over the Workers connect API so drivers like aiomysql and asyncpg work unchanged, enabling the Hyperdrive integration.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Unmodified database driver support reduces switching costs to Cloudflare's serverless database stack.
insights.locator: The second is a socket bridge

insights.claim: Cloudflare proposed PEP 783 standardising PyEmscripten, a platform for Python in browser runtimes, which was accepted after more than a year, ending Cloudflare's role as the sole compiler and host of native-extension wheels.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Removes a vendor bottleneck on package availability, broadening the WebAssembly Python ecosystem.
insights.locator: The first is a packaging standard

insights.claim: Cloudflare stabilised the Pyodide build toolchain and added PyEmscripten support to cibuildwheel so maintainers can build their own wheels.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Ecosystem-level investment benefits competing WebAssembly runtimes too.
insights.locator: The first is a packaging standard

themes.theme: Cold start and runtime cost debate

insights.claim: Wasmer founder Syrus Akbary said a minimal Python app started in about 60ms on Wasmer Edge versus about 900ms on Cloudflare Workers in a benchmark his company published, and that sub-100ms startup will be hard with Cloudflare's current architecture.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A competitor claims a ~15x cold-start advantage; latency-sensitive workloads may favour rivals. Source is a competing vendor.
insights.quote: It will be quite hard for them to achieve <100ms startup time with their current architecture.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's Dominik Picheta said the memory snapshot implementation has improved cold starts significantly and sharding reduces how often cold starts occur, though Akbary noted the earlier post reported about 1.027 seconds startup.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Cold-start performance remains unquantified publicly, a key adoption risk.
insights.quote: Our memory snapshot implementation has improved the cold starts significantly already.
insights.locator: Dominik Picheta, one of the post's authors

insights.claim: Compatibility flags select Python 3.12, 3.13 or 3.14, but older versions bring older Pyodide releases with fewer features, which Akbary saw as confirming version coupling to workerd.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Runtime version lock-in could limit enterprise adoption.
insights.locator: Version coupling was Akbary's other objection

insights.claim: A commenter speculated Python Workers likely consume tens of MBs more of worker memory allocation, untested.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Memory overhead affects unit economics of Python on edge serverless.
insights.quote: This likely eats in 10's of MBs more into the worker memory allocation.

insights.claim: Cloudflare says only that it plans to make Python Workers more performant and memory-efficient, publishing no new performance figures.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Absence of numbers suggests performance is still a work in progress.

insights.claim: A urllib3 maintainer said Cloudflare-related funding went to the contributor implementing Pyodide/Emscripten support rather than to the maintainers left holding it.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Highlights open-source sustainability risk underpinning commercial cloud runtimes.
insights.quote: There is a meaningful difference between funding a contribution to an upstream project and funding the upstream maintainers.
insights.locator: The third item drew the sharpest response

insights.claim: urllib3's Emscripten backend remains experimental and out of scope of its security policy, and CVE-2025-50182 showed redirect controls misbehaving when requests are routed through fetch, with more such differences possible.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Security gaps in shimmed networking layers are a latent risk for production users.
insights.locator: The consequence shows in urllib3's own posture

insights.claim: Two of the three authors of the announcement maintain Pyodide: Gyeongjae Choi is a Pyodide core developer and Hood Chatham is a Pyodide contributor Cloudflare hired.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is directly funding the core runtime it depends on, mitigating some upstream risk.
insights.locator: The same thread carries the counterweight

insights.claim: The author concludes the GA label settles less than the engineering beneath it, leaving open who maintains upstream pieces over time and what the runtime costs at startup and in memory.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: GA status does not remove maintenance and performance uncertainties.
insights.quote: the GA label settles less than the engineering beneath it
